newsitem.title: CHINA: Central China train crash kills 67, injures 260.
newsitem.headline: Central China train crash kills 67, injures 260.

text.p: A crowded passenger train ploughed into the back of a stationary train in China's central Hunan province on Tuesday, killing 67 people and injuring more than 260, local officials said.
The crash occurred in late morning at Rongjiawan station on China's trunk line linking the capital, Beijing, with the southern boomtown of Guangzhou, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Local officials said the death toll had risen to 67 people by 1.00 a.m. on Wednesday (1700 GMT), with more than 260 injured, including at least 90 in serious condition.

Xinhua had earlier placed the death toll at 90 with 300 injured but later revised the number of deaths down to 58 by 10.00 p.m. (1400 GMT), quoting Liao Jiguang, director of the Guangzhou Railway Administration.
Xinhua gave no new figure for the injured.

The No 324 train, travelling north from the southwestern city of Kunming, capital of Yunnan province, to Zhengzhou, capital of central Henan province, crashed into the rear of the stationary train, the agency said.
The stationary train was the No 818 en route from the Hunan town of Linxiang to the provincial capital, Changsha.
The collision derailed 13 carriages, a station official in Rongjiawan, some 1,350 km (840 miles) south of Beijing, said by telephone.
More than 1,100 police and medical workers had rushed to the scene to help with rescue work, the official said.
Hospitals at Rongjiawan were packed with injured and some had even been sent to the city of Yueyang, 50 km (30 miles) to the north, for treatment.
An official at a hospital in Rongjiawan said about 120 of the injured had been admitted, of whom two had since died. An estimated 50 to 60 were in serious condition, she said.
"There are alot of broken bones and some head injuries," she said.
Another 40 casualties were being treated at a hospital in Yueyang county, officials said. "We received about 40 injured and three of them have died," one hospital official said.
An official of the Number One People's Hospital in the nearby city of Yueyang said eight seriously injured patients from the crash had been admitted.
"There are many, many people injured," she said.

Officials said the cause of the crash was under investigation but preliminary reports showed failure to switch the points for the Kunming to Zhengzhou train was to blame. It was not yet known if human error was to blame, they said.
Traffic on the main Beijing-Guangzhou line was unaffected because trains had been switched to the three other tracks, local officials said.
Officials were reluctant to give details of the crash, which comes less than a month after China upgraded the speed of its trains that have for years travelled at a snail's pace.

China's trains accelerated on April 1, with those on the main Beijing-Guangzhou line speeding up to 140 kph (84 mph) -- the fastest in China -- from a previous 97.6 kph (58.5 mph), officials have said.
Rail remains the most popular method of transport in China and China's trains are usually extremely crowded with long-distance trains carrying as many as 1,000 passengers.
Safety on China's railways has improved in recent years after a series of bloody crashes in the mid-1980s when hundreds of people were killed.
